fields.name: Hand Weapon
fields.bodyIndex: Even the most poorly prepared warrior will arm themselves with a hand weapon, such as a simple sword or axe. It may even be that the model's natural weapons, such as teeth and claws, fulfil this role. Regardless of the form it takes, almost every model, even a cavalry mount, is considered to be armed with a hand weapon with the following profile: - Notes: Unless specified otherwise, all models are assumed to be equipped with a hand weapon.

content.value: Hand weapons

fields.name: Thrusting Spear

content.value: The favoured weapon of massed infantry regiments. Although too long to be used effectively on the charge, thrusting spears are the ideal defensive weapon. Their length enables their wielders to fight in multiple ranks whilst keeping the enemy at a (comparatively) safe distance and robbing them of their impetus, forcing them to battle past jabbing spear tips to close the distance.

fields.bodyIndex: Fight In Extra Rank Notes: Models whose troop type is infantry only. A model wielding a thrusting spear cannot make a supporting attack during a turn in which it charged. During a turn in which it was charged in its front arc, a model wielding a thrusting spear gains a +1 modifier to its Initiative against the charging unit(s).

content.value: thrusting spears

fields.name: Light Armour
fields.bodyIndex: Armour Value: 6+ Representing incomplete suits of mail, occasional plates of armour and even the thick, calloused hides of some creatures, light armour offers a degree of protection to vital areas.

content.value: light armour

fields.name: Shield
fields.bodyIndex: A shield may be a simple wooden board, or it may be an ornate and finely decorated thing – layers of wood, leather and resin trimmed and faced with beaten metal and finished with carefully painted symbols and heraldry. Whatever form it takes, shields are carried by warriors of all races. A model that carries a shield improves its armour value by 1. For example, a model equipped with light armour has an armour value of 6+. Should that model also carry a shield, its armour value would be improved by 1 by lowering the target number from 6+ to 5+. Note that if a model uses a weapon that has the Requires Two Hands special rule in combat, it cannot also use a shield.

content.value: shields

fields.name: Close Order

content.value: The mainstay of any army is its regiments of close order infantry and cavalry.

fields.bodyIndex: A unit consisting of models with this special rule may adopt a Close Order formation.

fields.name: Elven Reflexes

content.value: Elves possess phenomenal speed and grace, striking at their enemies faster than the eye can see.

fields.bodyIndex: A model with this special rule (but not its mount) has a +1 modifier to its Initiative characteristic (to a maximum of 10) during the first round of any combat.

content.value: Elven Reflexes

content.value: Elven warriors
spend many hours mastering the art of war, wielding their weapons with a skill and grace absent from the ranks of their enemies.

fields.bodyIndex: A unit with this special rule can make supporting attacks to its flank or rear, as well as to its front.

fields.bodyIndex: A unit with this special rule can be accompanied by detachment.
